title: 4.3 prompt-chaining / nullable-fields
stem: The moderation system uses tool_use with a JSON schema for classification output. All fields including 'sub_category' and 'target_demographic' are marked as required. Auditors discover that when a post is spam (which has no target demographic), the model fabricates plausible-sounding demographics like 'general public' or 'young adults.' What schema change prevents this fabrication?

options.A: Add a validation step that rejects target_demographic values for spam posts
options.B: Make 'target_demographic' nullable so the model can return null when the field is not applicable, rather than being forced to fabricate a value
options.C: Remove 'target_demographic' from the schema entirely since it causes fabrication
options.D: Add a prompt instruction telling the model to leave target_demographic empty for spam posts

why_correct: Required fields pressure the model to produce a value even when none exists. Making the field nullable gives the model a legitimate way to indicate 'not applicable,' eliminating the incentive to fabricate. This is the standard pattern for fields that apply conditionally.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Post-hoc validation catches the problem but does not prevent it. The model still fabricates values; they are just rejected after the fact. Schema design should prevent fabrication at the source.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Removing the field loses valuable data for categories where target demographic is genuinely relevant (hate speech, harassment). The fix is making it nullable, not removing it.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Prompt instructions cannot override a schema that marks the field as required. The JSON schema enforces the constraint at the API level, and the model must comply with the schema regardless of prompt instructions.

exam_takeaway: Required fields pressure the model to produce a value even when none exists. Making the field nullable gives the model a legitimate way to indicate 'not applicable,' eliminating the incentive to fabricate. This is the standard pattern for fields that apply conditionally.

sources.label: Lesson 4.2: Structured Output with Tool Use (Nullable fields)

title: 4.3 prompt-chaining / enum-fields
stem: The moderation system's classification schema has a 'category' field defined as a free-text string. Auditors find 47 different category values in production data, including 'hate speech', 'Hate Speech', 'hate-speech', 'hateful content', and 'hate_speech' — all intended to be the same category. This makes downstream analytics and routing unreliable. What is the best schema fix?

options.A: Add a post-processing normalisation step that maps all variations to canonical category names
options.B: Change the 'category' field from free-text string to an enum with predefined values like 'hate_speech', 'spam', 'harassment', and include an 'other' option for edge cases
options.C: Add detailed instructions to the prompt listing the exact category names to use and their formatting
options.D: Add few-shot examples showing the correct category formatting for each type

why_correct: Enum fields constrain the model to predefined values, eliminating spelling and formatting variations. Including 'other' as an enum value handles edge cases without allowing free-text drift. With strict: true, the schema guarantees only valid enum values are returned.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Post-processing normalisation adds complexity and requires constant maintenance as new variations appear. The schema should prevent the problem at the source rather than patching it downstream.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Prompt instructions are probabilistic. The model may still produce variations despite instructions. Schema-level enforcement via enums is deterministic and cannot be overridden.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Few-shot examples improve consistency but cannot guarantee exact string matching. Schema enums are the correct mechanism for constraining categorical output to a fixed set of values.

exam_takeaway: Enum fields constrain the model to predefined values, eliminating spelling and formatting variations. Including 'other' as an enum value handles edge cases without allowing free-text drift. With strict: true, the schema guarantees only valid enum values are returned.

sources.label: Lesson 4.2: Structured Output with Tool Use (Enum schema)

title: 4.4 few-shot-examples / retry-boundary
stem: The moderation system validates that every classification includes a 'reasoning' field explaining the decision. When validation fails (empty reasoning), the system retries. For most posts, the retry succeeds after feeding back the error 'reasoning field was empty — provide a brief justification for the classification.' However, for posts in unfamiliar languages, retries consistently fail. What should the system do?

options.A: Increase the retry count from 1 to 5 for unfamiliar language posts since the model may succeed with more attempts
options.B: Apply the retry boundary principle: retry format errors (empty reasoning on posts the model can analyse) but route capability failures (unfamiliar languages) to human review instead of retrying
options.C: Add the unfamiliar language to the system prompt as a supported language to encourage the model to try harder
options.D: Remove the reasoning validation requirement for posts in unfamiliar languages

why_correct: The retry boundary distinguishes between fixable format issues and unfixable capability gaps. Empty reasoning on analysable posts is a format error that retries with error feedback can fix. Unfamiliar languages represent absent capability — no amount of retrying will create language understanding. Route these to human review.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: More retries are ineffective when the model lacks the capability to analyse content in that language. The failure is not a transient format issue — the model genuinely cannot provide reasoning for content it cannot understand.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Listing an unsupported language in the prompt does not give the model language understanding. This may actually worsen the problem by encouraging fabricated analysis of content the model cannot read.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Removing the validation requirement means these posts would receive classifications without any justification, which undermines auditability. The correct approach is human review, not lower standards.

exam_takeaway: The retry boundary distinguishes between fixable format issues and unfixable capability gaps. Empty reasoning on analysable posts is a format error that retries with error feedback can fix. Unfamiliar languages represent absent capability — no amount of retrying will create language understanding. Route these to human review.

sources.label: Lesson 4.3: Prompt Chaining and Validation-Retry (Retry boundary)

title: 4.4 few-shot-examples / detected-patterns
stem: A moderation classification tool includes a `detected_patterns` array where the model lists specific patterns it identified (e.g. 'repeated slur targeting ethnicity'). Validation checks whether the detected patterns match the assigned category, and on mismatch retries with feedback like 'You classified this as spam but detected patterns of hate speech targeting ethnicity, please re-evaluate.' What is the primary benefit of the `detected_patterns` field in this workflow?

options.A: It lets the system auto-correct the category by overriding the model's classification with a rule-based pattern match
options.B: It provides an auditable evidence trail showing which specific content features drove each moderation decision
options.C: It enables the validation step to detect internal reasoning inconsistencies and provide targeted error feedback that the model can use to self-correct its classification
options.D: It increases classification accuracy by forcing the model to identify specific patterns before assigning a category

why_correct: The detected_patterns field externalises the model's reasoning into structured data that can be programmatically validated against the conclusion. When patterns and category are inconsistent, the specific error feedback ('you detected hate speech patterns but classified as spam') gives the model actionable information to self-correct. This is the core benefit in a retry-with-error-feedback workflow.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: The system does not override the model's classification. It feeds back the inconsistency and asks the model to re-evaluate. The model may correct its category or its patterns — the point is self-correction, not rule-based override.
per_option_counter_explanations.B: Auditability is a secondary benefit. The primary benefit in this validation/retry workflow is enabling the system to detect and feed back reasoning inconsistencies for self-correction.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: While structured reasoning fields can improve accuracy, this framing misses the retry workflow context. The primary benefit is enabling programmatic validation of reasoning consistency and targeted feedback for self-correction.

exam_takeaway: The detected_patterns field externalises the model's reasoning into structured data that can be programmatically validated against the conclusion. When patterns and category are inconsistent, the specific error feedback ('you detected hate speech patterns but classified as spam') gives the model actionable information to self-correct. This is the core benefit in a retry-with-error-feedback workflow.

title: 4.6 output-validation / self-review-bias
stem: The moderation team asks a single Claude session to classify a post, then immediately asks the same session to independently review its own classification for quality assurance. The 'review' agrees with the original classification 98% of the time, including cases that human auditors later identify as errors. Why is this self-review ineffective?

options.A: The model needs a stronger review prompt with explicit instructions to look for errors in the original classification
options.B: The same session retains the reasoning context from the original classification — the model is anchored to its own reasoning and cannot independently re-evaluate the content. Use a separate agent instance with no access to the original classification for genuine independent review
options.C: The model's temperature is too low, producing deterministic agreement — increase temperature for the review pass
options.D: Self-review is effective but the 98% agreement rate simply reflects high initial accuracy — the 2% disagreement is the expected error rate

why_correct: Self-review within the same session is fundamentally limited because the model's conversation context includes the original reasoning. It will naturally be anchored to its prior conclusions. An independent instance with no access to the original decision evaluates the content fresh, providing genuine quality assurance.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Stronger instructions do not overcome the fundamental limitation. The same session retains the reasoning context from the original classification, biasing the review toward agreement.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Temperature affects sampling randomness, not reasoning independence. Higher temperature may occasionally produce different outputs but does not create genuine independent review. The model is still anchored to its own prior reasoning in the same session.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Human auditors found errors in cases where the self-review agreed, proving the 98% agreement does not reflect accuracy. The self-review is confirming errors, not catching them, due to same-session reasoning bias.

exam_takeaway: Self-review within the same session is fundamentally limited because the model's conversation context includes the original reasoning. It will naturally be anchored to its prior conclusions. An independent instance with no access to the original decision evaluates the content fresh, providing genuine quality assurance.

sources.label: Lesson 4.6: Multi-Instance Review and Output Validation (Self-review limitation)

title: 4.6 output-validation / multi-pass
stem: The moderation system processes batches of reported posts. Each post needs individual classification, but the team also wants to detect coordinated campaigns (many accounts posting similar violating content). What multi-instance architecture achieves both goals?

options.A: Process all posts in a single large prompt so the model can see patterns across posts and detect campaigns
options.B: Run per-post local classification passes for consistent individual analysis, then a separate cross-post integration pass that reviews the individual classifications to detect coordinated campaign patterns
options.C: Process posts in small batches of 5 to balance individual accuracy with campaign detection
options.D: Use two separate systems: one for individual classification and one for campaign detection, with no shared data

why_correct: Multi-pass architecture solves both needs. Per-post passes ensure consistent depth for each individual classification. The cross-post integration pass operates on the structured classification results to detect coordination patterns — similar content, timing, account relationships — without degrading individual classification quality.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: A single large prompt causes attention dilution. Per-post classification quality degrades for posts later in the sequence, and the model may miss individual violations while looking for cross-post patterns.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Small batches are a compromise that does neither task well. Batch processing still risks attention dilution for individual classification and limits campaign detection to only 5 posts at a time, missing broader coordination patterns.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Separate systems with no shared data means the campaign detection system cannot leverage the individual classifications. The multi-pass approach shares classification results from the local passes into the integration pass, which is essential for detecting coordination.

exam_takeaway: Multi-pass architecture solves both needs. Per-post passes ensure consistent depth for each individual classification. The cross-post integration pass operates on the structured classification results to detect coordination patterns — similar content, timing, account relationships — without degrading individual classification quality.

title: 5.1 context-window-management / facts-block
stem: A customer support agent handles a multi-issue session. After several turns, the agent refers to 'your recent refund request' instead of the specific $247.83 refund for order #8891. The conversation history is being summarised between turns to manage context length. What is the most effective fix?

options.A: Increase the context window size to avoid summarisation entirely
options.B: Extract transactional facts (amounts, dates, order numbers) into a persistent case facts block included in every prompt, outside summarised history
options.C: Instruct the model to preserve all numerical values during summarisation
options.D: Store the full conversation in an external database and retrieve relevant turns on demand

why_correct: This directly addresses the progressive summarisation trap by ensuring critical numerical and transactional data is never condensed.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: This postpones the problem but does not solve it — eventually the context will fill, and summarisation will still destroy specifics.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Prompt-based instructions for summarisation are unreliable — the model will still compress details probabilistically.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: This adds infrastructure complexity without addressing the core issue of which facts must persist in every prompt.

exam_takeaway: This directly addresses the progressive summarisation trap by ensuring critical numerical and transactional data is never condensed.

title: 5.2 prompt-caching / explicit-escalation
stem: A customer support agent achieves only 55% first-contact resolution, well below the 80% target. Logs show it escalates straightforward damage replacement cases while attempting to autonomously handle complex policy exception requests. What is the most effective improvement?

options.A: Implement sentiment analysis to detect customer frustration and automatically escalate when negative sentiment exceeds a threshold
options.B: Have the agent self-report a confidence score (1-10) and automatically route to humans when confidence falls below a threshold
options.C: Add explicit escalation criteria to the system prompt with few-shot examples demonstrating when to escalate versus resolve autonomously
options.D: Deploy a separate classifier model trained on historical tickets to predict which requests need escalation

why_correct: This directly addresses unclear decision boundaries with concrete examples. It is the proportionate first response before adding infrastructure.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Sentiment does not correlate with case complexity. This would escalate frustrated but straightforward cases and miss calm but complex ones.
per_option_counter_explanations.B: LLM self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated — the agent is already incorrectly confident on hard cases and uncertain on easy ones.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: This is over-engineered, requiring labelled data and ML infrastructure when prompt optimisation has not been tried first.

exam_takeaway: This directly addresses unclear decision boundaries with concrete examples. It is the proportionate first response before adding infrastructure.

sources.label: Lesson 5.2: Escalation and Ambiguity Resolution (Explicit escalation criteria)
Lesson 5.2: Escalation and Ambiguity Resolution (Valid escalation triggers)

title: 5.3 long-conversations / structured-error-context
stem: A web search subagent in a multi-agent research system times out while researching a complex topic. You need to design how this failure information flows back to the coordinator. Which approach best enables intelligent recovery?

options.A: Return structured error context including failure type, attempted query, partial results, and potential alternative approaches
options.B: Implement automatic retry with exponential backoff, returning a generic 'search unavailable' status only after all retries are exhausted
options.C: Catch the timeout and return an empty result set marked as successful
options.D: Propagate the timeout exception to a top-level handler that terminates the entire research workflow

why_correct: This gives the coordinator everything it needs to decide: retry with modified query, try an alternative approach, or proceed with partial results.

per_option_counter_explanations.B: The generic status hides valuable context from the coordinator, preventing informed recovery decisions.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Silent suppression prevents any recovery. The coordinator believes the search succeeded and found nothing, so it will not attempt alternatives.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Workflow termination wastes partial results from other subagents that may have completed successfully.

exam_takeaway: This gives the coordinator everything it needs to decide: retry with modified query, try an alternative approach, or proceed with partial results.

title: 5.4 rate-limiting-quotas / scratchpad
stem: A developer productivity agent is exploring an unfamiliar codebase. After investigating several modules, it starts referencing 'typical repository patterns' instead of the specific class names and dependency chains it discovered earlier. What is the most effective mitigation?

options.A: Increase the model's context window to accommodate more discovery output
options.B: Have the agent maintain scratchpad files recording key findings and reference them for subsequent questions
options.C: Restart the session and ask the agent to explore more efficiently
options.D: Pre-load the entire codebase structure into the initial context before exploration begins

why_correct: Scratchpad files persist knowledge across context boundaries, directly counteracting context degradation by keeping critical discoveries accessible.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Context degradation is not about running out of tokens — it is about the model losing grip on earlier findings as verbose output accumulates.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Restarting loses all accumulated knowledge without addressing the underlying context degradation problem.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: This would consume context budget before exploration even starts and does not address degradation during the session.

exam_takeaway: Scratchpad files persist knowledge across context boundaries, directly counteracting context degradation by keeping critical discoveries accessible.

title: 5.5 monitoring-observability / aggregate-metrics-trap
stem: A structured data extraction system achieves 97% overall accuracy across all document types. The team proposes automating all extractions where model confidence exceeds 95% to reduce human review costs. What is the critical risk in this approach?

options.A: The 95% confidence threshold is too low and should be raised to 99% for automation
options.B: Aggregate accuracy may mask poor performance on specific document types or fields, and confidence scores need calibration against labelled validation sets before use
options.C: The model will become overconfident over time as it processes more documents, requiring regular retraining
options.D: Automated extractions should always have human review regardless of confidence, making the proposal fundamentally flawed

why_correct: 97% overall can hide 40% error rates on specific document types. Without stratified validation and confidence calibration, automation will silently fail on certain inputs.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: The threshold value is not the core issue — the problem is that aggregate metrics hide per-type performance disparities.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: LLMs do not train during inference. The issue is existing calibration gaps, not drift.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Automation is valid when properly validated — the issue is doing it based on uncalibrated aggregate metrics, not the concept of automation itself.

exam_takeaway: 97% overall can hide 40% error rates on specific document types. Without stratified validation and confidence calibration, automation will silently fail on certain inputs.

title: 5.6 production-reliability / conflict-handling
stem: A multi-agent research system produces a synthesis report on market trends. Two credible sources report different growth rates for the same sector: Source A reports 12% growth (2023 data) and Source B reports 8% growth (2024 data). The synthesis agent currently selects the more recent value. What is the correct approach?

options.A: Always use the most recent source as it reflects the latest data
options.B: Average the two values and report 10% growth with a note about source variance
options.C: Annotate both values with source attribution and publication dates, letting the consumer decide how to interpret the difference
options.D: Flag the conflict and escalate to a human researcher for resolution before including in the report

why_correct: This preserves provenance, temporal context, and both data points. The consumer can see that different dates explain different numbers.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: This silently discards valid historical context. The difference may reflect an actual trend, not a contradiction.
per_option_counter_explanations.B: Averaging conflicting statistics is mathematically misleading and destroys the temporal context that explains the difference.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: This is unnecessary — the values are not contradictory, they reflect different time periods. Proper annotation resolves the ambiguity.

exam_takeaway: This preserves provenance, temporal context, and both data points. The consumer can see that different dates explain different numbers.

Lesson 5.6: Information Provenance and Multi-Source Synthesis (Temporal awareness)

title: 5.3 long-conversations / access-vs-empty
stem: A research subagent queries an academic journal database for articles on renewable energy policy. The database responds successfully but returns zero matching articles. Meanwhile, a second subagent querying a government statistics API receives a connection timeout. The coordinator currently handles both cases identically by retrying three times. What should change?

options.A: Increase the retry count to five for both cases to give transient failures more time to resolve
options.B: Add exponential backoff to all retries so the subagents wait progressively longer between attempts
options.C: Remove retries entirely and immediately escalate both failures to a human operator for investigation
options.D: Distinguish access failures from valid empty results: retry the API timeout as a transient failure, but accept the zero-match journal response as a valid finding and annotate the coverage gap

why_correct: Access failures (timeouts, connection errors) indicate the tool could not reach the data source and warrant retry. Valid empty results mean the tool reached the source and found no matches — this IS the answer. Conflating these leads to unnecessary retries on valid results and missed coverage annotations.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: More retries do not fix the core problem. The journal database returned a valid empty result — it successfully searched and found nothing. Retrying it wastes time and API calls on an operation that already completed correctly.
per_option_counter_explanations.B: Backoff improves retry behaviour for transient failures but does not address the fundamental issue: the journal query does not need retries at all. It returned a valid response indicating no matches exist.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: This is disproportionate. The API timeout is a transient failure that retries can resolve. The empty journal result is not a failure at all — it is a valid answer. Neither case requires human escalation.

exam_takeaway: Access failures (timeouts, connection errors) indicate the tool could not reach the data source and warrant retry. Valid empty results mean the tool reached the source and found no matches — this IS the answer. Conflating these leads to unnecessary retries on valid results and missed coverage annotations.

title: 5.5 monitoring-observability / stratified-sampling
stem: A legal document extraction pipeline has been running for three months with calibrated confidence thresholds. Extractions above 90% confidence are auto-approved without human review, saving 60% of reviewer time. A new client submits contracts written in an unusual two-column legal format the system has not encountered before. The system reports 92% confidence on these extractions. What is the appropriate safeguard?

options.A: Maintain stratified random sampling of high-confidence extractions across document types, which would detect the elevated error rate on the new format before significant damage occurs
options.B: Trust the calibrated confidence threshold since it was validated against labelled data and the system reports 92% confidence, which exceeds the 90% auto-approval threshold
options.C: Raise the confidence threshold from 90% to 98% for all document types to account for novel formats
options.D: Add a document format classifier that flags unknown formats for mandatory human review before any auto-approval

why_correct: Stratified random sampling is designed precisely for this scenario: detecting novel error patterns in high-confidence extractions that slip past threshold-based routing. By sampling across document types, the new format's errors would surface during routine verification even though the confidence scores appear acceptable.

per_option_counter_explanations.B: Confidence calibration is only valid for document types represented in the calibration data. A novel format the system has never encountered can produce miscalibrated confidence scores — the model may be systematically overconfident because it does not recognise its own unfamiliarity with the format.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Raising the threshold globally penalises well-understood document types that are genuinely accurate at 90%+. This wastes reviewer capacity on documents that do not need review, while still not guaranteeing detection of format-specific issues.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: While not wrong in principle, this adds ML infrastructure complexity that stratified sampling already handles. A format classifier requires training data and maintenance, whereas ongoing stratified sampling detects novel error patterns without additional models.

exam_takeaway: Stratified random sampling is designed precisely for this scenario: detecting novel error patterns in high-confidence extractions that slip past threshold-based routing. By sampling across document types, the new format's errors would surface during routine verification even though the confidence scores appear acceptable.

sources.label: Lesson 5.5: Human Review and Confidence Calibration (Stratified sampling)

title: 5.6 production-reliability / claim-source-mapping
stem: A multi-agent research system has three subagents (financial filings, news, technical white papers) and a synthesis agent. Each subagent returns properly attributed findings, but the final synthesised report has no source attribution: stakeholders cannot trace which claim came from which source. Which fix addresses the root cause?

options.A: Append a bibliography section at the end of the report listing all sources each subagent consulted
options.B: Have each subagent include source URLs as inline hyperlinks in their prose output so the synthesis agent can preserve them
options.C: Require subagents to output structured claim-source mappings (claim, source URL, document name, excerpt, publication date) and instruct the synthesis agent to preserve and merge these mappings through the synthesis process
options.D: Store all subagent outputs in a database and have the synthesis agent reference database entries by ID instead of incorporating content directly

why_correct: Structured claim-source mappings survive synthesis because they are data structures, not prose that gets rewritten. The synthesis agent can merge mappings from multiple subagents while preserving the link between each claim and its source. This also enables content-appropriate rendering: financial data as tables, news as prose, technical findings as lists — each with attribution intact.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: A bibliography lists sources but does not map specific claims to specific sources. Stakeholders need to know which claim came from which document, not just which documents were consulted overall. This is document-level attribution, not claim-level provenance.
per_option_counter_explanations.B: Inline hyperlinks in prose are fragile — the synthesis agent will rewrite, merge, and compress prose during summarisation, stripping or disconnecting links from their associated claims. Attribution must be in structured data, not embedded in prose that gets rewritten.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: This adds infrastructure complexity without solving the synthesis problem. The synthesis agent still needs to merge and present findings coherently. Database references do not prevent attribution loss during the summarisation and rewriting that synthesis inherently requires.

exam_takeaway: Structured claim-source mappings survive synthesis because they are data structures, not prose that gets rewritten. The synthesis agent can merge mappings from multiple subagents while preserving the link between each claim and its source. This also enables content-appropriate rendering: financial data as tables, news as prose, technical findings as lists — each with attribution intact.

title: 5.1 context-window-management / progressive-summarisation
stem: What is the 'progressive summarisation trap' in the context of managing long conversations with Claude?

options.A: The model progressively ignores older messages in the conversation, regardless of summarisation
options.B: Each round of summarisation compresses specific details (amounts, dates, identifiers) into generic references, permanently destroying critical information
options.C: The model produces increasingly shorter summaries over time, eventually reducing context to a single sentence
options.D: Summarisation causes the model to hallucinate facts that were not in the original conversation

why_correct: Progressive summarisation destroys specifics because each compression round replaces concrete values like '$247.83 for order #8891' with generic phrases like 'recent refund'. This information loss is cumulative and irreversible.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: This describes general attention degradation, not the specific summarisation trap. The trap is about what happens when summarisation is actively applied, not passive attention loss.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: The trap is not about summary length decreasing. Summaries may stay a consistent length while still losing critical specific details in favour of generic language.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: While hallucination can occur, the progressive summarisation trap specifically refers to the loss of real specifics, not the introduction of false ones.

exam_takeaway: Progressive summarisation destroys specifics because each compression round replaces concrete values like '$247.83 for order #8891' with generic phrases like 'recent refund'. This information loss is cumulative and irreversible.

sources.label: Lesson 5.1: Context Window Management (Progressive summarisation)

title: 5.2 prompt-caching / cache-layout
stem: When using prompt caching with the Claude API, what is the correct ordering of content within the prompt to maximise cache hit rates?

options.A: Dynamic user content first, then static system instructions, with the cache breakpoint at the end
options.B: Static system prompt content first, cache_control breakpoint after the static section, then dynamic content last
options.C: Interleave static and dynamic content throughout the prompt, placing cache breakpoints after each static section
options.D: Place all content in a single block with no breakpoints and let the API determine optimal caching automatically

why_correct: Prompt caching matches from the beginning of the prompt. Static content first ensures the prefix remains identical across requests. The cache breakpoint marks where caching ends, and dynamic content after it does not affect cache validity.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Placing dynamic content first invalidates the cache on every request because the prefix changes. Caching works by matching from the beginning of the prompt forward.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Interleaving dynamic content breaks the cache prefix. The cache matches from the start, so any dynamic content before a static section invalidates the cache for everything after it.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Prompt caching requires explicit cache_control breakpoints. Without them, caching is not applied and every request is processed from scratch.

exam_takeaway: Prompt caching matches from the beginning of the prompt. Static content first ensures the prefix remains identical across requests. The cache breakpoint marks where caching ends, and dynamic content after it does not affect cache validity.

title: 5.3 long-conversations / scratchpad
stem: What is the primary purpose of scratchpad files in the context of long-running Claude Code agent sessions?

options.A: They serve as temporary storage for code changes before committing to version control
options.B: They persist key findings and discoveries across context boundaries so the agent can reference them when earlier conversation content degrades
options.C: They allow multiple agents to share state by reading and writing to a common file
options.D: They provide a log of all tool calls made during a session for debugging purposes

why_correct: Scratchpad files solve context degradation by externalising critical knowledge to the filesystem. When the agent's context window fills and earlier findings become unreliable, the scratchpad provides a persistent, accurate reference.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Scratchpad files in the agent context are not about version control staging. They address the problem of context window limitations during extended exploration.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: While agents could theoretically share files, the primary purpose of scratchpad files is to help a single agent maintain continuity across its own context boundaries, not inter-agent communication.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Scratchpad files are for preserving discovered knowledge, not logging tool calls. Tool call logs serve a different observability purpose.

exam_takeaway: Scratchpad files solve context degradation by externalising critical knowledge to the filesystem. When the agent's context window fills and earlier findings become unreliable, the scratchpad provides a persistent, accurate reference.

title: 5.5 monitoring-observability / confidence-calibration
stem: In a data extraction pipeline, what does 'confidence calibration' mean and why is it required before automating decisions based on confidence scores?

options.A: It means training the model to always output confidence scores above 90% so that most extractions can be automated
options.B: It means verifying that when the model reports X% confidence, approximately X% of those predictions are actually correct, validated against labelled data
options.C: It means adjusting the model's temperature parameter until confidence scores fall within an acceptable range
options.D: It means running the same extraction multiple times and averaging the confidence scores to reduce variance

why_correct: Calibration ensures the model's reported confidence matches its actual accuracy. If 90% confidence predictions are only correct 60% of the time, the scores are miscalibrated and automating based on them will produce unacceptable error rates.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Calibration is about the accuracy of confidence scores, not about raising them. A model that outputs 90% confidence on everything is poorly calibrated, not well calibrated.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Temperature affects output randomness, not confidence calibration. Calibration requires empirical validation against ground truth data, not parameter tuning.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Repeated runs measure consistency, not calibration. A model can consistently report 95% confidence and consistently be wrong — that is consistent but poorly calibrated.

exam_takeaway: Calibration ensures the model's reported confidence matches its actual accuracy. If 90% confidence predictions are only correct 60% of the time, the scores are miscalibrated and automating based on them will produce unacceptable error rates.

title: 5.4 rate-limiting-quotas / retry-strategy
stem: A customer support agent system encounters API rate limits from the Claude API during a peak traffic period. Multiple concurrent user sessions are failing. What is the recommended retry strategy?

options.A: Retry immediately at fixed intervals until the request succeeds
options.B: Exponential backoff with jitter, increasing wait times between retries to allow the rate limit to reset
options.C: Switch to a different API key to bypass the rate limit
options.D: Queue all requests and process them in a single batch after a fixed 60-second delay

why_correct: Exponential backoff progressively increases wait times, reducing pressure on the API. Jitter prevents multiple clients from synchronising their retries and creating burst patterns.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Fixed-interval immediate retries can worsen rate limiting by maintaining constant pressure on the API. This may extend the rate limit period.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: This circumvents rather than manages rate limits. It violates API terms of service and does not address the underlying capacity issue.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: A fixed 60-second delay is arbitrary and does not adapt to the actual rate limit window. It also creates poor user experience for latency-sensitive support interactions.

exam_takeaway: Exponential backoff progressively increases wait times, reducing pressure on the API. Jitter prevents multiple clients from synchronising their retries and creating burst patterns.

title: 5.1 context-window-management / token-budget
stem: A customer support agent uses a token budget of 200k tokens. The system prompt consumes 8k tokens, conversation history takes 120k tokens, and the most recent tool call result returned 65k tokens. The agent is struggling to produce thorough responses. What is the most likely cause and fix?

options.A: The model is running out of response tokens — system prompt (8k) + history (120k) + tool result (65k) = 193k, leaving only 7k for the response. Summarise conversation history or truncate verbose tool results to free up response budget
options.B: The system prompt is too large at 8k tokens and should be reduced to under 2k to leave more room for the response
options.C: The model needs a higher max_tokens parameter to produce longer responses
options.D: The conversation history should be cleared entirely to give the model a fresh context for each response

why_correct: Token budget is shared: system prompt + conversation history + tool results + available for response = total budget. With 193k consumed, only 7k remains for the response. The fix targets the largest movable allocations: summarise older history or trim verbose tool output.

per_option_counter_explanations.B: The system prompt at 8k is a small fraction of the budget. Reducing it by 6k would help marginally but misidentifies the problem — conversation history and tool results are consuming the vast majority of the budget.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: max_tokens caps the response length but cannot exceed the remaining context budget. If 193k of 200k is consumed by input, increasing max_tokens beyond 7k would have no effect.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Clearing history would free tokens but destroy conversation continuity. The customer would need to repeat their issue. Selective summarisation is far preferable to wholesale deletion.

exam_takeaway: Token budget is shared: system prompt + conversation history + tool results + available for response = total budget. With 193k consumed, only 7k remains for the response. The fix targets the largest movable allocations: summarise older history or trim verbose tool output.

title: 5.2 prompt-caching / cache-strategy
stem: A structured data extraction pipeline processes 500 documents per hour. Each request sends the same 12k-token system prompt with extraction schemas, followed by the document content which varies per request. The team wants to reduce API costs. Which prompt caching strategy is most effective?

options.A: Cache the entire prompt including document content, since many documents have similar structures
options.B: Place the 12k-token system prompt and extraction schemas first, set a cache_control breakpoint after them, then append the variable document content. The static prefix caches across all 500 requests per hour
options.C: Send the document content first so the model processes it before the extraction instructions, then cache the extraction schemas at the end
options.D: Split each request into two API calls: one for the cached system prompt and one for the document, then combine the results

why_correct: The 12k static prefix is identical across all requests and caches effectively. At 500 requests per hour, the cache read savings on 12k tokens per request significantly reduces costs. Variable document content after the breakpoint does not affect cache validity.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Document content varies per request. Caching the entire prompt would result in near-zero cache hits because the full prompt changes with every document.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: This inverts the correct ordering. Cache matching works from the beginning of the prompt forward. Placing variable content first means the prefix changes every request, defeating caching entirely.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: The API does not support splitting a single inference across two calls this way. Prompt caching handles this natively within a single request by distinguishing cached and uncached portions.

exam_takeaway: The 12k static prefix is identical across all requests and caches effectively. At 500 requests per hour, the cache read savings on 12k tokens per request significantly reduces costs. Variable document content after the breakpoint does not affect cache validity.

title: 5.4 rate-limiting-quotas / batch-vs-realtime
stem: A multi-agent research system has two types of workloads: real-time user queries requiring sub-5-second responses, and nightly batch jobs that process 10,000 documents for indexing. Both currently use the same API tier and compete for the same rate limits. During nightly batch runs, user query latency spikes to 30+ seconds. What is the correct architectural fix?

options.A: Increase the rate limit by upgrading to a higher API tier so both workloads have sufficient capacity
options.B: Separate the workloads: use the batch processing API for the nightly indexing jobs (optimised for throughput, not latency) and reserve the real-time API tier for user queries (optimised for latency)
options.C: Throttle the batch job to process only 100 documents per hour during business hours to leave capacity for user queries
options.D: Queue user queries during batch processing and respond to them when the batch completes

why_correct: Batch processing APIs are designed for high-throughput, latency-tolerant workloads. Real-time APIs prioritise low latency. Separating workloads ensures user queries are not starved by batch operations and batch jobs benefit from throughput optimisations.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: A higher tier increases overall capacity but does not prevent batch jobs from consuming all available throughput. The fundamental issue is workload competition, not total capacity.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Throttling reduces batch throughput without fully solving the problem. The batch job still competes for the same rate limits, and the arbitrary throttle may not match actual user query demand patterns.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Queueing user queries violates the sub-5-second latency requirement. Users waiting for responses while a multi-hour batch runs is an unacceptable user experience.

exam_takeaway: Batch processing APIs are designed for high-throughput, latency-tolerant workloads. Real-time APIs prioritise low latency. Separating workloads ensures user queries are not starved by batch operations and batch jobs benefit from throughput optimisations.

title: 5.6 production-reliability / claim-source-mapping
stem: A data extraction pipeline extracts financial figures from annual reports. The pipeline cites sources using inline text references like 'According to page 12 of the 2024 Annual Report, revenue was $4.2B.' When the extracted data is consumed by a downstream analytics system, the source attribution is consistently lost. What is the root cause and fix?

options.A: The downstream system strips text formatting. Fix by making the citations bold or using a special delimiter
options.B: Inline prose citations are fragile because downstream systems rewrite, parse, or restructure text. Fix by outputting structured claim-source mappings where each extracted value is paired with its source document, page, and date as structured data fields
options.C: The downstream system needs to be modified to preserve all input text verbatim without any transformation
options.D: Add a separate attribution database that the downstream system can query to look up sources for any extracted value

why_correct: Structured claim-source mappings survive downstream processing because they are data fields, not prose. An analytics system can consume {'value': '4.2B', 'source': '2024 Annual Report', 'page': 12} without losing attribution, whereas it will discard 'According to page 12...' during text processing.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: The problem is not formatting but data structure. Regardless of text formatting, inline prose citations are lost when text is parsed, summarised, or restructured by downstream systems.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Requiring downstream systems to preserve verbatim text is impractical and fragile. Systems legitimately need to transform, aggregate, and restructure data. Attribution should be in a format that survives transformation.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: While a database could store attributions, this adds unnecessary infrastructure when the extraction pipeline can simply output structured mappings directly. The attribution should travel with the data, not require a separate lookup.

exam_takeaway: Structured claim-source mappings survive downstream processing because they are data fields, not prose. An analytics system can consume {'value': '4.2B', 'source': '2024 Annual Report', 'page': 12} without losing attribution, whereas it will discard 'According to page 12...' during text processing.

title: 5.5 monitoring-observability / aggregate-metrics-trap
stem: A structured data extraction system processes invoices, purchase orders, and contracts. The monitoring dashboard shows 97% overall extraction accuracy and the team considers the system production-ready. A detailed audit reveals: invoices 99.5% accuracy (80% of volume), purchase orders 98% accuracy (15% of volume), contracts 72% accuracy (5% of volume). What does this reveal and what action is required?

options.A: The system is performing well. 72% on contracts is acceptable since contracts represent only 5% of volume and barely affect the overall metric
options.B: The aggregate accuracy metric is masking a severe per-type performance disparity. Contracts need mandatory human review until accuracy improves, and monitoring must report per-type metrics alongside aggregate figures
options.C: The training data needs rebalancing so that contracts represent a larger proportion, which will naturally improve contract accuracy
options.D: The 97% threshold should be raised to 99% overall to force improvement across all document types

why_correct: This is a textbook case of aggregate metrics hiding per-type problems. 97% overall is misleading because high-volume invoice accuracy (99.5%) overwhelms the poor contract performance (72%). Per-type metrics would have surfaced this immediately. Contracts need different treatment until the extraction quality is acceptable.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Acceptability depends on the business impact, not volume percentage. Contract extraction errors may have severe financial or legal consequences despite low volume. A 28% error rate on any document type is significant.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: LLMs used for extraction are not retrained on production data this way. The issue is monitoring visibility and operational response, not model training data distribution.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Raising the aggregate threshold does not address per-type disparities. Even at 99% overall, contract accuracy could remain low if invoice volume continues to dominate the metric. The solution is per-type metrics, not a higher aggregate bar.

exam_takeaway: This is a textbook case of aggregate metrics hiding per-type problems. 97% overall is misleading because high-volume invoice accuracy (99.5%) overwhelms the poor contract performance (72%). Per-type metrics would have surfaced this immediately. Contracts need different treatment until the extraction quality is acceptable.

sources.label: Lesson 5.5: Human Review and Confidence Calibration (Aggregate metrics trap)

title: 5.3 long-conversations / context-degradation
stem: A multi-agent system runs a 45-minute deep research workflow. Around the 30-minute mark, the coordinator's synthesis quality drops: it refers to 'the key findings' instead of specific statistics it cited earlier, and misattributes a claim from the financial subagent to the news subagent. No token limits or errors have been hit. What is the most likely diagnosis and correct mitigation?

options.A: The model is experiencing 'fatigue' from a long session and needs a cooldown period before continuing
options.B: Context degradation: the accumulated conversation has pushed early subagent results far back in the context, reducing the model's effective attention to those details. Implement periodic context consolidation that extracts key findings into a structured summary block placed near the end of the context
options.C: The token limit has been silently exceeded and the API is truncating early messages. Upgrade to a larger context window model
options.D: The subagents are returning inconsistent data, confusing the coordinator. Add data validation to each subagent's output before it reaches the coordinator

why_correct: Context degradation occurs when important information is buried deep in a long conversation. The model's attention to early content diminishes as new content accumulates. Consolidating key findings into a recent, structured block keeps them in the model's effective attention window without losing the specifics.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: LLMs do not experience fatigue. Each inference is independent. The degradation is caused by context window dynamics, not model tiredness.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: The question states no token limits have been hit. Context degradation occurs well before token limits are reached — it is an attention quality issue, not a capacity issue.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: The coordinator previously cited these same findings correctly earlier in the session. The issue is not data quality from subagents but the coordinator's degrading attention to that data over time.

exam_takeaway: Context degradation occurs when important information is buried deep in a long conversation. The model's attention to early content diminishes as new content accumulates. Consolidating key findings into a recent, structured block keeps them in the model's effective attention window without losing the specifics.

title: 5.6 production-reliability / conflict-handling
stem: A multi-agent research system finds conflicting data on a pharmaceutical compound's efficacy. A 2022 peer-reviewed clinical trial reports 78% efficacy, while a 2024 preprint reports 45% efficacy with a larger sample size. The synthesis agent must produce a recommendation for a medical advisory board. Which approach correctly handles the conflicting sources?

options.A: Use the 2024 preprint as it has a larger sample size and is more recent, noting it supersedes the 2022 study
options.B: Average the two values (61.5%) and present it as the best estimate with a note about variance between studies
options.C: Present both findings with full provenance: source identity, publication date, peer-review status, sample size, methodology, and any methodological differences that may explain the discrepancy. Let the advisory board weigh the evidence
options.D: Exclude both findings and report that no reliable consensus exists, recommending further research before any conclusions

why_correct: For a medical advisory board, preserving full provenance is critical. The board needs to weigh peer-review status, sample size, methodology differences, and temporal context. Annotating both sources with complete metadata enables informed human judgment on conflicting scientific evidence.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Recency and sample size alone do not determine reliability. The preprint has not undergone peer review, and simply picking one source discards valuable context that the advisory board needs for informed decision-making.
per_option_counter_explanations.B: Averaging conflicting scientific results is methodologically invalid. The studies may have different populations, methodologies, or endpoints. The average has no scientific meaning and obscures the actual disagreement.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Excluding available evidence is unhelpful. The advisory board can make informed decisions with properly attributed conflicting data. Withholding findings because they conflict reduces the board's ability to assess the situation.

exam_takeaway: For a medical advisory board, preserving full provenance is critical. The board needs to weigh peer-review status, sample size, methodology differences, and temporal context. Annotating both sources with complete metadata enables informed human judgment on conflicting scientific evidence.

title: 5.1 context-window-management / token-budget
stem: In Claude's token budget, which components compete for space within the context window?

options.A: Only the user's message and the model's response share the context window; system prompts and tool results are handled separately
options.B: System prompt, conversation history, tool call results, and the tokens available for the model's response all share a single context window budget
options.C: The system prompt has its own dedicated allocation that does not affect the tokens available for conversation or response
options.D: Tool call results are streamed separately and do not consume context window tokens

why_correct: The context window is a single shared budget. System prompt tokens + conversation history tokens + tool result tokens + response tokens must all fit within the total window. Over-allocating to any component reduces what is available for others.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: System prompts and tool results are part of the context window. All input tokens, regardless of source, consume context budget.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: There is no separate allocation for system prompts. A 10k-token system prompt consumes 10k tokens from the same shared budget, leaving less for conversation and response.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Tool results are injected into the context as part of the conversation. They consume tokens from the same shared context window as everything else.

exam_takeaway: The context window is a single shared budget. System prompt tokens + conversation history tokens + tool result tokens + response tokens must all fit within the total window. Over-allocating to any component reduces what is available for others.

sources.label: Lesson 5.1: Context Window Management (Token budget components)

title: 5.4 rate-limiting-quotas / batch-vs-realtime
stem: A support system processes two request types: password resets (high volume, latency-sensitive, customers wait on screen) and account migrations (low volume, complex, can complete overnight). Both share one synchronous API endpoint at identical priority. At peak hours, migrations consume rate limit capacity and password-reset latency exceeds thresholds. What is the best approach?

options.A: Pause all account migration requests during business hours and process them only between midnight and 6am
options.B: Route password resets through the real-time API for low-latency responses, and route account migrations through the batch processing API for high-throughput, latency-tolerant processing
options.C: Implement a priority queue where password resets always execute before migration requests, using a single API endpoint
options.D: Add more API keys to increase total rate limit capacity so both workloads can run simultaneously without contention

why_correct: This matches each workload to the appropriate API tier. Password resets need low latency and get real-time processing. Migrations tolerate latency and benefit from batch throughput. The workloads no longer compete for the same rate limits.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: A fixed time window is inflexible and may not align with actual demand patterns. It also delays migrations unnecessarily during off-peak hours when capacity is available.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: A priority queue on a single endpoint still means both workloads compete for the same rate limit. If the queue is full of migrations, new resets still experience latency waiting for in-flight migration requests to complete.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Multiple API keys to increase rate limits may violate terms of service and does not fundamentally solve the architectural mismatch between latency-sensitive and throughput-oriented workloads.

exam_takeaway: This matches each workload to the appropriate API tier. Password resets need low latency and get real-time processing. Migrations tolerate latency and benefit from batch throughput. The workloads no longer compete for the same rate limits.

title: 5.2 prompt-caching / ambiguous-matching
stem: A customer support agent searches for a customer named 'Sarah Johnson' and the lookup tool returns three matching accounts with the same name but different addresses and account ages. The agent selects the most recently active account and proceeds with the refund. Later, the customer calls back because the refund was applied to the wrong account. What should the agent have done differently?

options.A: Selected the account with the oldest creation date, as long-standing customers are more likely to be the caller.
options.B: Asked the customer for additional identifying information — email address, phone number, or order number — to disambiguate the matching accounts.
options.C: Processed the refund across all three accounts to ensure the correct customer received it.
options.D: Escalated to a human agent immediately because the system returned ambiguous results.

why_correct: When multiple customers match a search query, the agent must ask for additional identifiers rather than selecting based on heuristics. This ensures the correct account is identified before any action is taken.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Account age is an unreliable heuristic for identifying the correct customer. Any selection based on heuristics risks choosing the wrong account.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Processing refunds on incorrect accounts creates financial discrepancies and additional work to reverse the erroneous transactions. The agent must identify the correct account first.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Ambiguous search results are a routine scenario that the agent can resolve by asking for clarification. Escalation is not warranted when the agent can gather additional information to disambiguate.

exam_takeaway: When multiple customers match a search query, the agent must ask for additional identifiers rather than selecting based on heuristics. This ensures the correct account is identified before any action is taken.

sources.label: Lesson 5.2: Escalation and Ambiguity Resolution (Ambiguous customer matching)

title: 5.2 prompt-caching / explicit-escalation
stem: A customer says: 'This is ridiculous, I have been waiting 20 minutes. Just connect me to a real person.' The agent has access to the customer's account and can see the issue is a simple password reset that takes 30 seconds to resolve. What should the agent do?

options.A: Acknowledge the frustration and offer to resolve the password reset, explaining it will take only 30 seconds — the issue is straightforward and escalation is unnecessary.
options.B: Escalate to a human agent immediately without attempting to resolve the issue, because the customer explicitly requested a human.
options.C: Run sentiment analysis to confirm the customer is genuinely frustrated before deciding whether to escalate or attempt resolution.
options.D: Ask the customer if they would prefer to wait for a human or let the agent resolve the password reset quickly.

why_correct: When a customer explicitly says 'connect me to a real person', the agent must escalate immediately. This is one of the three valid escalation triggers. The simplicity of the issue is irrelevant — the customer's explicit request takes priority.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: The customer has explicitly requested a human agent. Regardless of how simple the issue is, the agent must honour the explicit request immediately. Attempting to resolve first ignores the customer's stated preference.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Sentiment analysis is an unreliable escalation trigger. More importantly, the customer's explicit request for a human is the trigger here, not their emotional state. Sentiment analysis adds unnecessary processing.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: The customer has already stated their preference clearly. Asking again ignores their explicit request and adds friction to an already frustrating experience.

exam_takeaway: When a customer explicitly says 'connect me to a real person', the agent must escalate immediately. This is one of the three valid escalation triggers. The simplicity of the issue is irrelevant — the customer's explicit request takes priority.

title: 5.1 context-window-management / tool-result-trimming
stem: An analytics agent queries Snowflake and receives 40+ columns per row, only 5 of which are relevant to the user's question about quarterly revenue. The agent appends the full result set to context. After three such queries the window is nearly full and follow-up questions fail. What is the most effective fix?

options.A: Upgrade to a model with a larger context window so that full result sets can be accommodated across more queries.
options.B: Trim tool results to only the relevant columns before appending them to the conversation context.
options.C: Store all query results in an external database and have the agent retrieve specific values on demand instead of keeping results in context.
options.D: Limit the number of rows returned by each query to reduce the total data volume in context.

why_correct: Tool result trimming removes irrelevant fields before they enter the context window. Keeping only the 5 relevant columns from each 40+ column result set dramatically reduces token consumption, allowing the agent to handle many more queries within the same context budget.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: A larger context window postpones the problem but does not solve it. Each full result set still wastes tokens on 35+ irrelevant columns, and the context will eventually fill regardless of size.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: External storage adds infrastructure complexity without addressing the core issue. The agent still needs some result data in context to reason about it. Trimming irrelevant fields is simpler and directly reduces context consumption.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Row limits reduce data volume but may exclude relevant rows. The problem is column-level verbosity (35+ irrelevant columns per row), not row count. Trimming columns preserves all relevant rows whilst eliminating irrelevant fields.

exam_takeaway: Tool result trimming removes irrelevant fields before they enter the context window. Keeping only the 5 relevant columns from each 40+ column result set dramatically reduces token consumption, allowing the agent to handle many more queries within the same context budget.

sources.label: Lesson 5.1: Context Window Management (Tool result trimming)

title: 5.3 long-conversations / silent-suppression
stem: A multi-agent system has subagents for web search, academic database, and industry reports. The academic database subagent hits a 403 Forbidden on a specific journal, catches the error, and returns an empty result set marked as successful. The coordinator produces a final report with no academic sources. What is the critical failure in this design?

options.A: The coordinator should validate that all subagents return non-empty results before producing the final report.
options.B: The subagent silently suppressed the access failure by returning empty results as success, preventing the coordinator from attempting recovery or noting the gap in coverage.
options.C: The subagent should have retried the request with exponential backoff, as 403 errors are often transient.
options.D: The entire workflow should have been terminated when the academic database subagent encountered the 403 error.

why_correct: Silent suppression — returning empty results marked as success — is the worst error propagation anti-pattern. The coordinator believes the academic search succeeded and found nothing, so it produces a report without academic sources and without noting the coverage gap. The subagent should have returned structured error context with the failure type, what was attempted, and potential alternatives.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Requiring non-empty results from all subagents would cause the workflow to fail when a subagent legitimately finds no matching data. The issue is that the error was suppressed, not that the coordinator failed to validate result volume.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: 403 Forbidden is a permission error, not a transient error. Retrying will not resolve it — the subagent lacks the required access credentials. The correct response is to propagate the error with its type so the coordinator knows the failure is not retryable.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Workflow termination on a single subagent failure wastes partial results from the web search and industry reports subagents that may have completed successfully. The coordinator should proceed with available results and annotate the coverage gap.

exam_takeaway: Silent suppression — returning empty results marked as success — is the worst error propagation anti-pattern. The coordinator believes the academic search succeeded and found nothing, so it produces a report without academic sources and without noting the coverage gap. The subagent should have returned structured error context with the failure type, what was attempted, and potential alternatives.

sources.label: Lesson 5.3: Error Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems (Silent suppression anti-pattern)

title: 5.4 rate-limiting-quotas / subagent-delegation
stem: Claude Code is auditing API documentation coverage across a large codebase. After exploring 15 modules, the agent produces vague references like 'the authentication module follows standard patterns' instead of citing specific class names and method signatures it discovered earlier. `/compact` has already been used once. What is the most effective next step?

options.A: Run /compact again to further reduce context usage and continue the exploration in the same session.
options.B: Delegate remaining module explorations to subagents, providing each with a summary of findings so far from a scratchpad file, while the main agent preserves coordination context.
options.C: Start a fresh session and re-explore all 15 modules more efficiently to rebuild the context with only essential findings.
options.D: Increase the model's temperature to encourage more detailed and specific outputs instead of vague pattern references.

why_correct: Subagent delegation isolates verbose exploration output from the main agent's context. The scratchpad file persists specific findings (class names, method signatures) across context boundaries. The main agent retains enough context for coordination without being overwhelmed by discovery output.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Running /compact again may help marginally, but the fundamental problem is that the agent's context has filled with verbose discovery output from 15 modules. Compacting alone does not restore the specific findings that have been lost to context degradation.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: Re-exploring 15 modules wastes significant time and effort. The specific findings from earlier exploration are lost. A scratchpad file would have preserved them, and subagent delegation prevents the problem going forward.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: Temperature affects output randomness, not the model's ability to recall specific findings from earlier in a long context. The problem is context degradation from verbose output accumulation, not generation settings.

exam_takeaway: Subagent delegation isolates verbose exploration output from the main agent's context. The scratchpad file persists specific findings (class names, method signatures) across context boundaries. The main agent retains enough context for coordination without being overwhelmed by discovery output.

sources.label: Lesson 5.4: Codebase Exploration and Context Degradation (Subagent delegation)
Lesson 5.4: Codebase Exploration and Context Degradation (Scratchpad files)

title: 5.5 monitoring-observability / per-field-calibration
stem: A contract extraction system reports 96% overall accuracy. The team plans to auto-approve all extractions where model confidence exceeds 90%. A pilot reveals party name extraction achieves 99% accuracy but indemnification clause extraction only 71%, even though the model reports high confidence on both. What should they implement before automating?

options.A: Raise the automation confidence threshold from 90% to 99% to ensure only the most reliable extractions are automated.
options.B: Calibrate confidence thresholds per field type using labelled validation sets, and implement stratified sampling to continuously monitor accuracy by document type and field segment.
options.C: Exclude indemnification clauses from automation entirely and continue automating all other field types at the 90% threshold.
options.D: Train a separate classification model to predict extraction accuracy before deciding whether to automate each extraction.

why_correct: Field-level confidence calibration using ground truth data exposes the discrepancy between reported confidence and actual accuracy. Stratified sampling provides ongoing monitoring to detect novel error patterns. Together, these ensure automation is only applied where validated accuracy justifies it.

per_option_counter_explanations.A: Raising the threshold does not fix the calibration problem. The model reports high confidence even for indemnification clauses where it achieves only 71% accuracy. Raw confidence scores are unreliable without calibration.
per_option_counter_explanations.C: This addresses the known problem but does not detect future calibration issues with other field types. Without systematic calibration and monitoring, other fields with hidden accuracy problems will be automated incorrectly.
per_option_counter_explanations.D: A separate model adds infrastructure complexity when the solution is to calibrate the existing confidence scores against labelled data. Calibration directly addresses the unreliable confidence outputs without requiring additional ML infrastructure.

exam_takeaway: Field-level confidence calibration using ground truth data exposes the discrepancy between reported confidence and actual accuracy. Stratified sampling provides ongoing monitoring to detect novel error patterns. Together, these ensure automation is only applied where validated accuracy justifies it.
